body:
Fixes #14.

Container scans now keep discovered objects visible when Docker size queries fail, distinguish writable cache data from immutable image data, and recover liveness inspection through a privileged read-only probe when ordinary root exec cannot inspect `/proc`. Unavailable probes still block cleanup, and incomplete Docker discovery returns a nonzero CLI status.

The changes also address the other cleanup and reporting gaps from the issue:

- Match process executables and interpreter scripts without treating arbitrary `.bun`/npm path arguments as running tools. Long-lived npm exec servers protect their active npx hash through command paths, cwd and open files, while idle npm/node-gyp caches and other aged hashes remain eligible. npm install still blocks the relevant caches.
- Count changed writable-layer file blocks and mounted data, including an identifiable Docker container used as the host environment. Report image bytes separately, keep image-only candidates visible and blocked, and show small stopped containers that pin large images.
- Remove opam download-cache files directly without invoking migration-capable `opam clean`. Add aged isolation logs, sanitized upload staging, and superseded Claude Code and Copilot CLI versions, with current/newest/in-use protection and cleanup-time version rechecks.
- Include candidates and blockers in scan audits without adding blocked bytes to reclaimable totals. Group repeated image hints, show watched process names and PIDs, and summarize investigation holds. The opt-in `--investigation-max-age` lifts old holds while retaining removal consent and Git checks.
- Inspect stopped-container Git work during plain scans. Recognize unstaged/untracked content preserved byte-for-byte, including modes, on one cached remote ref. Exclude nested Docker layer copies and temporary Codex plugin checkouts, and accept detached upstream commits only when reachable from a remote ref. Unpushed commits, stashes, staged changes, missing refs and mismatching files remain protected.

Reproduction and validation:

- Added focused regressions in `tests/issue-14-{liveness,docker,caches,storage,git}.test.js`. The original implementation failed the process matching, partial Docker discovery, opam/version/log discovery, writable accounting and recovery-ref reproductions before their fixes.
- `node experiments/issue-14-container.mjs` reproduces root `/proc/1/cwd` denial with a non-dumpable process, verifies the privileged inspection fallback, and confirms that 4 MiB of image cache plus 1 MiB of writable cache reports and frees exactly 1 MiB. The fixture has finite inputs, a process memory limit, and cleanup.
- `node experiments/issue-14-git-copy.mjs` checks 20 copied detached-repository states through a symlinked temporary directory, including Node 24 with Git 2.55. Fixture commands disable automatic maintenance so a background writer cannot remove `objects/maintenance.lock` during a copy. Container Git inspection failures include stack details with `DSS_DEBUG=1` or `--verbose`.
- Local Linux process inspection skips zombies before reading their command metadata. The regression checks that live command paths are retained, and `node experiments/issue-14-process-probe.mjs` measures three finite, read-only probes on a busy host.
- The full Node suite also runs with `node --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-timeout=30000 tests/*.test.js` using Node 24 and Git 2.55 on the long-lived local host, whose hundreds of zombie processes make concurrent process probes slow. Test deadlines remain unchanged. `bun test --timeout 30000`, `deno test --allow-read`, `npm run test:dind`, and `npm run check` cover the other runtimes, nested Docker cleanup and stopped-container Git protection. Syntax, file line limits and required-document checks also pass.

Writable-layer sizes are estimates of file blocks and mounted data; directory metadata is excluded. In-container host accounting requires identifying the container and reaching its Docker daemon. Recovery recognition uses cached remote refs and performs no network fetch; unavailable evidence leaves the original blocker in place.

The [final CI run](https://github.com/link-foundation/disk-space-saviour/actions/runs/37740286982) passes all nine Node/Bun/Deno platform combinations, Docker-in-Docker integration, and repository checks. The security, example-app and link-check workflows also pass. Final local results are 746 Node tests, 746 Bun tests, and 643 Deno tests plus eight steps, with no failures.

Includes one minor changeset for the new cleanup rules and investigation-age option; package versioning remains with the release workflow.
title: Fix container cleanup inspection, reclaimable accounting and missed caches
